strengths: The row update preserves orthogonality and supports inexpensive partial-gradient computation. The sufficient-decrease argument is useful and valid conditional on exact subproblem minimization.
Considering both rotations and reflections provides a useful two-row formulation for nonsmooth optimization, with potentially practical one-dimensional subproblem solvers.

The experiments cover ten datasets, three PCA formulations, multiple ranks and regularization strengths, and working-set variants. Comparisons include ManPG for ℓ1 regularization and show substantial objective improvements on several instances.
weaknesses: The central claim that BS2 stationarity implies criticality (Theorem 3.6(a)) is false under the stated assumptions. Equations (31)–(32) incorrectly replace a potentially different subgradient for each block with one common subgradient. A counterexample uses n=r=3, q=1/√2, X=[[0,q,q],[q,-1/2,1/2],[q,1/2,-1/2]], Ω=(1/4)[[0,1,-1],[-1,0,0],[1,0,0]], and S=sign(X), with S11=0. Set f(Y)=⟨ΩX−S,Y⟩ and h(Y)=||Y||1. Every two-row orthogonal update has F(Y)≥F(X): rotation increments are bounded below by (q−1/2)|sin θ| for pairs involving row 1 and by zero otherwise; reflection increments are nonnegative. Thus X is BS2 for Q=0 and any α>0. However, every subgradient is G=ΩX+zE11, z∈[-1,1], and criticality simultaneously requires z=−q and z=q. This directly invalidates the claimed optimality hierarchy, even with convex ℓ1 regularization and linear f.

The KL convergence proof contains independent substantive errors. Equation (48) exchanges the previously selected block with a fresh random block despite the dependence of X^{t+1} on the previous selection. Equations (53)–(54) also incorrectly replace a root-mean-square block norm with its mean. For n=3, r=1, k=2, X=e1, f(x)=x2, and h=0, the claimed full-residual bound becomes 1≤√(2/3), which is false. Consequently, Theorem 4.8 is not established.

The cyclic complexity result in Theorem 4.2(c) is unsupported. Equation (42) bounds updates evaluated at different iterates during a cycle; this does not establish the all-block stationarity measure at the single endpoint X^{kz}. An argument controlling residual changes across the cycle is missing.

The exact subproblem solver is incorrect as written. Section 5 and Appendix B list x_i/y_i as a zero of x_i+t y_i; the correct breakpoint is −x_i/y_i. Furthermore, dropping coordinates with y_i=0 is invalid for the ℓ1 problem because |x_i|/√(1+t²) still depends on t. These errors require correction and implementation validation before the exactness assumption can support the algorithmic guarantees.

The empirical evidence does not establish the broader claims about escaping poor local minima or general scalability. Results rely on short time budgets without reported repeated-run variability, stationarity certificates, or detailed baseline tuning. Warm-start improvements need matched-total-time controls. All experiments use k=2 and PCA variants, while efficient global solution for general k and h is assumed rather than demonstrated. These limitations matter, although the decisive concern is the failure of the central theoretical claim.
